entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.1-1Chr.26.3">1Ch 26:1-3</reference> <hi type="italic">The classes of the doorkeepers, the stewards of the treasures of the sanctuary, and the officers for the external business</hi>. - Vv. 1-19. <hi type="italic">The classes of the doorkeepers</hi>. 1Ch 26:1. The superscription runs shortly thus: “As to (ל) the divisions of the doorkeepers.” The enumeration beings with לקרחים: to the Korahites (belongs) Meshelemiah (in <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.14">1Ch 26:14</reference>, Shelemiah). Instead of אסף מן־בּני we should read, according to <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.19">1Ch 9:19</reference>, אביסף מן־בּני, for the Korahites are descended from Kohath (<reference osisRef="Exod.6.21">Exo 6:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="Exod.18.16">Exo 18:16</reference>), but Asaph is a descendant of Gershon (1Ch 6:39.). - In <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.2">1Ch 26:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.3">1Ch 26:3</reference>, seven sons of Meshelemiah are enumerated; the first-born Zechariah is mentioned also in <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.21">1Ch 9:21</reference>, and was entrusted, according to <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.14">1Ch 26:14</reference>, with the guarding of the north side.

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.4-1Chr.26.7">1Ch 26:4-7</reference> <div eID="gen5854" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5855" type="x-p"/> Obed-edom’s family. Obed-edom has been already mentioned in <reference osisRef="1Chr.16.38">1Ch 16:38</reference> and <reference osisRef="1Chr.15.24">1Ch 15:24</reference> as doorkeeper; see the commentary on the passage. From our passage we learn that Obed-edom belonged to the Kohathite family of the Korahites. According to <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.19">1Ch 26:19</reference>, the doorkeepers were Korahites and Merarites. The Merarites, however, are only treated of from <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.10">1Ch 26:10</reference> and onwards. אדם וּלעבד (<reference osisRef="1Chr.26.4">1Ch 26:4</reference>) corresponds to ולמשׁלמיהוּ (<reference osisRef="1Chr.26.2">1Ch 26:2</reference>), and is consequently thereby brought under לקּרהים (<reference osisRef="1Chr.26.1">1Ch 26:1</reference>). Here, <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.4">1Ch 26:4</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.5">1Ch 26:5</reference>, eight sons with whom God had blessed him (cf. <reference osisRef="1Chr.13.14">1Ch 13:14</reference>), and in <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.6">1Ch 26:6</reference> and <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.7">1Ch 26:7</reference> his grandchildren, are enumerated. The verb נולד is used in the singular, with a subject following in the plural, as frequently (cf. Ew. §316, <hi type="italic">a</hi>). The grandchildren of Obed-edom by his first-born son Shemaiah are characterized as המּמשׁלים, the dominions, i.e., the lords (rulers) of the house of their fathers (ממשׁל, the abstract dominion, for the concrete משׁל; cf. Ew. §160, <hi type="italic">b</hi>), because they were חיל גּבּורי, valiant heroes, and so qualified for the office of doorkeepers. In the enumeration in <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.7">1Ch 26:7</reference>, the omission of the ו cop. with אחיו אלזבד is strange; probably we must supply ו before both words, and take them thus: And Elzabad and his brethren, valiant men, (viz.) Elihu and Semachiah. For the conjecture that the names of the אחיו are not given (Berth.) is not a very probable one.

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.10-1Chr.26.11">1Ch 26:10-11</reference> <div eID="gen5856" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5857" type="x-p"/> The Merarites. Hosah’s sons and brothers. חוסה has been already mentioned (<reference osisRef="1Chr.16.38">1Ch 16:38</reference>) along with Obed-edom as doorkeeper. Hosah made Shimri head of the Merarites, who served as doorkeepers, because there was no first-born, i.e., because his first-born son had died without leaving any descendant, so that none of the families descended from Hosah had the natural claim to the birthright. All the sons and brothers of Hosah were thirteen. Meshelemiah had eighteen (cf. <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.9">1Ch 26:9</reference>), and Obed-edom sixty-two (<reference osisRef="1Chr.26.8">1Ch 26:8</reference>); and all taken together they make ninety-three, whom we are (according to 1Ch 26:12.) to regard as the heads of the 4000 doorkeepers. In <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.22">1Ch 9:22</reference> the number of the doorkeepers appointed by David is stated to be 212, but that number most probably refers to a different time (see on <reference osisRef="1Chr.9.22">1Ch 9:22</reference>). Bertheau further remarks: “According to <reference osisRef="1Chr.16.38">1Ch 16:38</reference>, sixty-eight are reckoned to Obed-edom and Hosah, in our passage seventy-five; and the small difference between the numbers is explained by the fact that in the first passage only the doorkeepers before the ark are referred to.” Against this we have already shown, in our remarks on <reference osisRef="1Chr.16.38">1Ch 16:38</reference>, that the number there mentioned cannot be held with certainty to refer to the doorkeepers.

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.12">1Ch 26:12</reference> <div eID="gen5857" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5858" type="x-p"/> The division of the doorkeepers according to their posts of service. 1Ch 26:12. “To these classes of doorkeepers, viz., to the heads of the men, (were committed) the watches, in common with their brethren, to serve in the house of Jahve.” By מחלקות לאלּה it is placed beyond doubt that the above-mentioned names and numbers give us the classes of the doorkeepers. entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.16">1Ch 26:16</reference> <div eID="gen5861" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5862" type="x-p"/> The word לשׁפּים is unintelligible, and probably has come into the text merely by a repetition of the two last syllables of the preceding word, since the name שׁפּים   (<reference osisRef="1Chr.7.12">1Ch 7:12</reference>) has no connection with this passage. To Hosah fell the lot towards the west, by the door Shallecheth on the ascending highway. העולה המסלּה is the way which led from the lower city up to the more lofty temple site. Instead of the door on this highway, in <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.18">1Ch 26:18</reference>, in the statement as to the distribution of the guard-stations, Parbar is named, and the highway distinguished from it, four doorkeepers being appointed for the מסלּה, and two for פּרבּר. פּרבּר .פּר, probably identical with פּרורים,   2Ki 23:11, a word of uncertain meaning, was the name of an out-building on the western side, the back of the outer court of the temple by the door Shallecheth, which contained cells for the laying up of temple goods and furniture. שׁלּכת, Böttcher translates, <hi type="italic">Proben</hi>, S. 347, “refuse-door;” see on 2Ki 23:11. Nothing more definite can be said of it, unless we hold, with Thenius on 2Ki 23:11, that Ezekiel’s temple is in all its details a copy of the Solomonic temple, and use it, in an unjustifiable way, as a source of information as to the prae-exilic temple. משׁמר לעמּת משׁמר (as in <reference osisRef="Neh.12.24">Neh 12:24</reference>), guard with (over against?) guard, or one guard as the other (cf. on לעמּת, <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.12">1Ch 26:12</reference> and <reference osisRef="1Chr.25.8">1Ch 25:8</reference>), Bertheau connects with Hosah, according to the Masoretic punctuation, and explains it thus: “Because it was Hosah’s duty to set guards before the western gate of the temple, and also before the gate Shallecheth, which lay over against it.” Clericus, on the contrary, refers the words to all the guard-stations: <hi type="italic">cum ad omnes januas essent custodiae, sibi ex adverso respondebant</hi>. This reference, according to which the words belong to what follows, and introduce the statement as to the number of guards at the individual posts which follows in 1Ch 26:17., seems to deserve the preference. So much is certain in any case, that there is no ground in the text for distinguishing the gate Shallecheth from the western gate of the temple, for the two gates are not distinguished either in <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.16">1Ch 26:16</reference> or in 1Ch 26:18.

Nothing more definite can be said of it, unless we hold, with Thenius on 2Ki 23:11, that Ezekiel’s temple is in all its details a copy of the Solomonic temple, and use it, in an unjustifiable way, as a source of information as to the prae-exilic temple. משׁמר לעמּת משׁמר (as in Neh 12:24 ), guard with (over against?) guard, or one guard as the other (cf. on לעמּת, 1Ch 26:12 and 1Ch 25:8 ), Bertheau connects with Hosah, according to the Masoretic punctuation, and explains it thus: “Because it was Hosah’s duty to set guards before the western gate of the temple, and also before the gate Shallecheth, which lay over against it.” Clericus, on the contrary, refers the words to all the guard-stations: cum ad omnes januas essent custodiae, sibi ex adverso respondebant . This reference, according to which the words belong to what follows, and introduce the statement as to the number of guards at the individual posts which follows in 1Ch 26:17., seems to deserve the preference. So much is certain in any case, that there is no ground in the text for distinguishing the gate Shallecheth from the western gate of the temple, for the two gates are not distinguished either in 1Ch 26:16 or in 1Ch 26:18.

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.17-1Chr.26.18">1Ch 26:17-18</reference> <div eID="gen5862" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5863" type="x-p"/> Settlement of the number of guard-stations at the various sides and places. Towards morning (on the east side) were six of the Levites (six kept guard); towards the north by day (i.e., daily, on each day), four; towards the south daily, four; and at the storehouse two and two, consequently four also; at Parbar towards the west, four on the highway and two at Parbar, i.e., six. In all, therefore, there were twenty-four guard-stations to be occupied daily; but more than twenty-four persons were required, because, even supposing that one man at a time was sufficient for each post, one man could not stand the whole day at it: he must have been relieved from time to time. Probably, however, there were always more than one person on guard at each post. It further suggests itself that the number twenty-four may be in some way connected with the divisions or classes of doorkeepers; but there is only a deceptive appearance of a connection. The division of the priests and musicians each into twenty-four classes respectively is no sufficient analogy in the case, for these classes had to perform the service in succession each for a week at a time, while the twenty-four doorkeepers’ stations had to be all occupied simultaneously every day. - In <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.2-1Chr.26.11">1Ch 26:2-11</reference>, then, twenty-eight heads in all are enumerated by name (Meshelemiah with seven sons, Obed-edom with eight sons and six grandsons, and Hosah with four sons); but the total number in all the three families of doorkeepers is stated at ninety-three, and neither the one nor the other of these numbers bears any relation to twenty-four. Finally, the posts are so distributed that Meshelemiah with his eighteen sons and brothers kept guard on the east and north sides with six posts; Obed-edom with his sixty-two sons and brothers on the south side with four and 2 x 2, that is, eight posts; and Hosah with his thirteen sons and brothers on the western side with four and two, that is, six; so that even here no symmetrical distribution of the service can be discovered.

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.20">1Ch 26:20</reference> <hi type="italic">The stewards of the treasures of the sanctuary.</hi> - <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.20">1Ch 26:20</reference> appears to contain the superscription of the succeeding section. For here the treasures of the house of God and the treasures of the consecrated things are grouped together, while in <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.22">1Ch 26:22</reference> and <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.26">1Ch 26:26</reference> they are separated, and placed under the oversight of two Levite families: the treasures of the house of Jahve under the sons of the Gershonite Laadan (<reference osisRef="1Chr.26.21">1Ch 26:21</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.22">1Ch 26:22</reference>); the treasures of the consecrated things under the charge of the Amramites. But with this the words אחיּה הלויּם cannot be made to harmonize. According to the Masoretic accentuation, הלויּם alone would be the superscription; but הלויּם alone gives no suitable sense, for the Levites have been treated of already from 1 Chron 23 onwards. Moreover, it appears somewhat strange that there is no further characterization of אחיּה, for the name is a very common one, but has not before occurred in our chapter, whence we would expect a statement of his descent and his family, such as we find in the case of the succeeding chief overseers. All these things tend to throw doubt upon the correctness of the Masoretic reading, while the lxx, on the contrary, in καὶ οἱ Δευῖται ἀδελφοὶ αὐτῶν ἐπὶ τῶν θησαυρῶν κ.τ.λ, give a perfectly suitable superscription, which involves the reading אחיהם instead of אחיּה. This reading we, with J. D. Mich. and Berth., hold to be the original. On אהיהם הלויּם, cf. <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.29">1Ch 6:29</reference>; 2Ch 29:34.

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.26-1Chr.26.28">1Ch 26:26-28</reference> <div eID="gen5864" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5865" type="x-p"/> This Shelomoth (a descendant of Eliezer, and so to be distinguished both from the Jisharite Shelomith <reference osisRef="1Chr.23.18">1Ch 23:18</reference> and <reference osisRef="1Chr.24.22">1Ch 24:22</reference>, and the Gershonite of the same name <reference osisRef="1Chr.23.9">1Ch 23:9</reference>), and his brethren were over the treasures of the consecrated things which David the king had consecrated, and the heads of the fathers'-houses, etc. Instead of לשׂרי we must read ושׁרי, according to 1Ch 29:6. The princes over the thousands and hundreds are the war captains, and the הצּבא שׂרי are the commanders-in-chief, e.g., Abner, Joab, <reference osisRef="1Chr.27.34">1Ch 27:34</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Sam.8.16">2Sa 8:16</reference>; 1Ch 18:15. - The 27th verse is an explanatory parenthesis: “from the wars and from the booty,” i.e., from the booty taken in war had they consecrated. לחזּק, to make strong, i.e., to preserve in strength and good condition the house of Jahve. חזּק elsewhere of the renovation of old buildings, 2Ki 12:8., Neh 3:2., here in a somewhat general signification. - In <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.28">1Ch 26:28</reference> the enumeration of those who had consecrated, thus interrupted, is resumed, but in the form of a new sentence, which concludes with a predicate of its own. In ההקדּישׁ the article represents אשׁר, as in <reference osisRef="1Chr.29.17">1Ch 29:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Chr.29.36">2Ch 29:36</reference>, and elsewhere; cf. Ew. §331, <hi type="italic">b</hi>. With המּקדּישׁ כּל, all who had consecrated, the enumeration is concluded, and the predicate, “was at the hand of Shelomith and his brethren,” is then brought in. על־יד, laid upon the hand, i.e., entrusted to them for preservation; Germ. <hi type="italic">unter der Hand</hi> (under the hand). <div eID="gen5865" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5866" type="x-p"/> If we glance back at the statements as to the stewards of the treasures (<reference osisRef="1Chr.26.20-1Chr.26.28">1Ch 26:20-28</reference>), we find that the treasures of the house of Jahve were under the oversight of the Jehielites Zetham and Joel, with their brethren, a branch of the Gershonites (v. 22); and the treasures of the consecrated things under the oversight of the Kohathite Shelomith, who was of the family of Moses’ second son Eliezer, with his brethren (v. 28). But in what relation does the statement in v. 24, that Shebuel, the descendant of Moses through Gershon, was על־האצרות נגיד, stand to this? Bertheau thinks “that three kinds of treasures are distinguished, the guarding of which was committed to different officials: (1) The sons of Jehieli, Zetham and Joel, had the oversight of the treasures of the house of God, which, as we may conclude from <reference osisRef="1Chr.29.8">1Ch 29:8</reference>, had been collected by voluntary gifts: (2) Shebuel was prince over the treasures, perhaps over the sums which resulted from regular assessment for the temple (<reference osisRef="Exod.30.11-Exod.30.16">Exo 30:11-16</reference>), from redemption-money, e.g., for the first-born (Num 18:16.), or for vows (Lev); consequently over a part of the sums which are designated in 2Ki 12:5 by the name הקדשים כסף: (3) Shelomith and his brothers had the oversight of all the הקדשים אוצרות, i.e., of the consecrated gifts which are called in 2Ki 12:19 קדשים, and distinguished from the קדשים כסף in 2Ki 12:5.” But this view has no support in the text. Both in the superscription (<reference osisRef="1Chr.26.20">1Ch 26:20</reference>) and in the enumeration (<reference osisRef="1Chr.26.22">1Ch 26:22</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.26">1Ch 26:26</reference>) only two kinds of treasures-treasures of the house of God (of Jahve), and treasures of the קדשׁים - are mentioned. Neither by the facts nor by the language used are we justified in supposing that there was a third kind of treasures, viz., the sums resulting from the regular assessment for the holy place. For it is thoroughly arbitrary to confine the treasures of the house of God to the voluntary contributions and the consecrated gifts given from the war-booty; and it is still more arbitrary to limit the treasures over which Shebuel was prince to the sums flowing into the temple treasures from the regular assessment; for the reference to 2Ki 12:19 and 2Ki 12:5 is no proof of this, because, though two kinds of קדשׁים are there distinguished, yet both are further defined. The quite general expression האצרות, the treasures, can naturally be referred only to the two different kinds of treasures distinguished in 1Ch 26:22. This reference is also demanded by the words נגיד...שׁבוּאל (<reference osisRef="1Chr.26.24">1Ch 26:24</reference>). Heads of fathers'-houses, with their brethren (אהיהם), are mentioned as guardians of the two kinds of treasures spoken of in <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.20">1Ch 26:20</reference>; while here, on the contrary, we have Shebuel alone, without assistants. Further, the other guardians are not called נגיד, as Shebuel is. The word נגיד denotes not an overseer or steward, but only princes of kingdoms (kings), princes of tribes (<reference osisRef="1Chr.12.27">1Ch 12:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Chr.13.1">1Ch 13:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Chr.27.16">1Ch 27:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Chr.32.21">2Ch 32:21</reference>), ministers of the palace and the temple, and commanders-in-chief (<reference osisRef="2Chr.11.11">2Ch 11:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Chr.28.7">2Ch 28:7</reference>), and is consequently used in our section neither of Zetham and Joel, nor of Shelomoth. The calling of Shebuel נגיד consequently shows that he was the chief guardian of the sacred treasures, under whose oversight the guardians of the two different kinds of treasures were placed. This is stated in <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.23">1Ch 26:23</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.24">1Ch 26:24</reference>; and the statement would not have been misunderstood if it had been placed at the beginning or the end of the enumeration; and its position in the middle between the Gershonites and the Kohathites is explained by the fact that this prince was, according to <reference osisRef="1Chr.23.16">1Ch 23:16</reference>, the head of the four Levite families descended from Kohath.

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="1Chr.26.29">1Ch 26:29</reference> <hi type="italic">The officials for the external business</hi>. - 1Ch 26:29. “As to the Izharites, Chenaniah (see on <reference osisRef="1Chr.15.22">1Ch 15:22</reference>) with his sons was for the outward business over Israel for scribes and judges.” According to this, the external business of the Levites consisted of service as scribes and judges, for which David had set apart 6000 Levites (<reference osisRef="1Chr.23.4">1Ch 23:4</reference>).
